hints: Focus on the direction you are asked for. Decomposition is the reverse of formation, so think about which species is the reactant and which is the product.
The formation has $\Delta H = -314$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, so it is exothermic. That means for decomposition the products must be higher in energy than the reactant.
Remember $E_A$ is always measured from the reactant level up to the top of the hump, while $\Delta H$ is measured from reactant level to product level.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction direction**

The question asks for decomposition, not formation. So the reactant is $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ on the left and the products are $\text{NH}_3 + \text{HCl}$ on the right.

$$\text{NH}_4\text{Cl(s)} \rightarrow \text{NH}_3\text{(g)} + \text{HCl(g)}$$

**Decide if it is exothermic or endothermic**

Formation is exothermic with $\Delta H = -314$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, so the reverse must be endothermic with $\Delta H = +314$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. In an endothermic profile the products finish higher than the reactants.

$$\text{products higher than reactant for endothermic}$$

**Check the labels for $\Delta H$ and $E_A$**

$\Delta H$ is the energy difference between reactant level and product level. $E_A$ is the energy difference between reactant level and the peak of the curve. Only the diagram that starts low with $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$, ends high with $\text{NH}_3 + \text{HCl}$, and draws both arrows up from the low reactant level is correct.

options.A: Energy levels are correct for endothermic decomposition, with $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ low and $\text{NH}_3 + \text{HCl}$ high. However $E_A$ is drawn from the product level to the peak instead of from the reactant level to the peak, so it is incorrectly labelled.
options.B: This shows endothermic decomposition correctly. $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ starts low, $\text{NH}_3 + \text{HCl}$ finishes high, $\Delta H$ goes from reactant to product, and $E_A$ goes from reactant to the peak. This matches the reverse of the exothermic formation.
options.C: This shows $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ high and $\text{NH}_3 + \text{HCl}$ low, which is the exothermic profile for formation, not decomposition. The question asks for decomposition which must go uphill in energy.
options.D: This also shows the wrong energy order for decomposition, with products lower than reactant. In addition $E_A$ is drawn from the low product level to the peak instead of from the high reactant level, so both the direction and the $E_A$ label are wrong.
